stories.headline: Uttar Pradesh elections: Samajwadi Party to release election manifesto on November 26
stories.title: Uttar Pradesh elections: Samajwadi Party to release election manifesto on November 26
stories.summary: It will include separate documents for women, youth and a manifesto on law and order, highlighting party’s commitment on these issues apart from focus on social justice and PDA plank
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Samajwadi Party (SP) will release its election manifesto for upcoming 2027 Assembly polls titled “Jan-Man Manifesto,” on November 26, 2026, coinciding with Constitution Day, a date of adoption of the Constitution of India in 1949.

The party president Akhilesh Yadav has announced that the party plans to release the proposed document, called the “Jan-Man Manifesto,” which will highlight outreach to backward classes, Dalits and minority communities.

“The manifesto will focus upon socially and economically marginalized section of the society, that includes women, backward classes, Scheduled Castes (SCs), Minorities and other neglected sections of the society.

We will also include separate documents for women, youth and a manifesto on law and order, it will include our commitment to various groups of people,” told Alok Ranjan, a former U.P. Chief Secretary, who closely worked with the party on policy issues.
After the release of this main manifesto, the party in coming weeks, will release region specific manifestos or district centric manifestos.

On asked about the manifesto release coinciding with the Constitution Day, Nasser Salim, the SP spokesperson said, “On Constitution Day, we reaffirm our faith in the Republic and in the sovereign will of the people.
This manifesto is not merely a political document but a public covenant inspired by the ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
It reflects our commitment to the constitutional empowerment of PDA and every citizen of India,”.
“Samajwadi Party firmly believes in the sanctity of the Indian Constitution which defines India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.
The SP has always stood for the fundamental rights and duties as enshrined in the constitution,” said Ram Pratap Singh, the SP spokesperson.

stories.headline: US Secretary of State Rubio lands in Mumbai for 3-day visit; trade deal, energy in focus
stories.title: US Secretary of State Rubio lands in Mumbai for 3-day visit; trade deal, energy in focus
stories.summary: Mumbai/New Delhi, Oct 20: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio kick-started a three-day visit to India on Tuesday to advance bilateral ties in energy, trade and investment, defence and critical technologies, and exchange views on the West Asia crisis. Rubio's second India visit this year comes amid persistent friction in bilateral ties. During his earlier trip in May, he held talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, besides attending a Quad foreign ministers' meeting. The visit of the US Secretary of State, who is accompanied by a large business delegation, is likely to focus largely on boosting India-US economic engagement. In their meeting in Mumbai on Tuesday afternoon, Jaishankar and Rubio are expected to deliberate on ways to further strengthen the India-US Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership. "Welcome to Mumbai, US Secretary of State, on your second visit to India!" Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal posted on social media shortly after the top American diplomat landed at the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport in India's financial capital. Rubio was received by Ashish Shelar, Maharashtra's Minister of Culture, Electronics, IT and AI, at the airport. "The visit provides an opportunity to further advance cooperation across the various pillars of the India-US Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership," Jaiswal said. In addition to his meeting with Jaishankar, Rubio's engagements in Mumbai included laying a wreath at the Taj memorial to honour the victims of the 26/11 terror attack, which claimed the lives of over 160 people, including six US nationals. The top American diplomat will also attend a reception to mark the 250th anniversary of the US' independence. "Discussions are expected to cover key areas of bilateral cooperation, including energy, trade and investment, defence, critical and emerging technologies, and other areas of mutual interest," Jaiswal said last week. The two sides are also likely to delve into the proposed bilateral trade deal as well as the situation in West Asia. "The visit will provide an opportunity to sustain the high-level engagement between the two countries and advance our shared priorities," Jaiswal had said. Rubio will travel to Jamnagar in Gujarat on Wednesday. Ahead of his visit, Rubio said in Uzbekistan that the US is "very close" to finalising the trade deal with India. He also suggested that the US waiver on tariffs for buying Russian oil was linked to the decision. Last week, US President Donald Trump suspended certain sanctions against Russia and five of the biggest buyers of Russian oil, including India. "We're trying to finalise the trade deal with India right now. We're very close to doing that. So that's one of the things we take into consideration when the President makes a decision about national security waivers and things of that nature," Rubio said. India and the US have been engaged in talks since early 2025 on the proposed trade pact to address tariff friction, eliminate non-tariff barriers, and boost bilateral market access. India is seeking better tariffs than its competitors for its goods in the US market. External Affairs Minister Jaishankar said a few days back that the trade talks between the two sides are nearing a "landing point". The India-US relations witnessed a major downturn after Washington imposed punitive tariffs on India last year and President Trump made assertions regarding his role in de-escalating the India-Pakistan military clashes of May 2025 that drew sharp reaction from Indian officials. Washington's new immigration policy and its decision to increase the H1B visa fee also contributed to the slide in India-US ties. The ties came under fresh strain after the US decided to restrict a key green-card processing programme for major global and Indian IT firms, including Tata Consultancy Services and Wipro.

stories.headline: Rubio, Jaishankar discuss energy security, defence ties amid continuing friction in India-US ties
stories.title: Rubio, Jaishankar discuss energy security, defence ties amid continuing friction in India-US ties
stories.summary: Mumbai/New Delhi, Oct 20: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Tuesday held wide-ranging talks largely focusing on cooperation in the energy and defence sectors against the backdrop of continuing friction in bilateral ties. The Jaishankar-Rubio meeting took place shortly after the top US diplomat landed in Mumbai on a three-day India visit that came nearly five months after his first trip to the country as the Secretary of State. Before his talks with Jaishankar, Rubio visited the Taj memorial and laid a wreath in honour of the victims of the horrific 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks that included six American citizens. "In Mumbai, Indian External Affairs Minister @DrSJaishankar and I discussed energy security and defense cooperation while reaffirming the importance of advancing the U.S.-India strategic partnership," the US Secretary of State said on social media. The top diplomat also answered questions from the media on the India-US energy ties as well as his trip to Reliance Industries Ltd's refinery in Jamnagar on Wednesday. "In order for energy to become usable, you have to refine it. You have a company with a massive amount of refining capability. I think I should go talk to them, especially when it involves nation-states," he said. "We're going to go see a company that has a tremendous amount of refining capability. It makes all the sense in the world to talk to them about it. It's very difficult to understand something or see what the possibilities are if you're not going to speak to them," he noted. The US Secretary of State also responded to a query on India's procurement of Russian crude oil. "India has expressed repeatedly its desire to diversify its energy portfolio, which is a smart thing to do. It's not easy to do that from one day to the next," he said. "I think they've made some substantial progress in that regard, and we're happy to see that. But in the end, it's not just about Russian oil; it's about India's desire to diversify, and we think we can be a source of some of its energy inputs." "We have discussed Venezuela and other countries, and I think it's in our interest to have strong allies with diverse energy portfolios," he noted. It is not immediately known whether the proposed trade deal between India and the US figured in the Rubio-Jaishankar talks. Ahead of his visit, Rubio said in Uzbekistan that the US is "very close" to finalising the trade deal with India. He also suggested that the US waiver on tariffs for buying Russian oil was linked to the decision. Last week, US President Donald Trump suspended certain sanctions against Russia and five of the biggest buyers of Russian oil including India. "We're trying to finalise the trade deal with India right now. We're very close to doing that. So that's one of the things we take into consideration when the President makes a decision about national security waivers and things of that nature," Rubio said on Monday. India and the US have been engaged in talks since early 2025 on the proposed trade pact to address tariff friction, eliminate non-tariff barriers and boost bilateral market access. India is seeking better tariffs than its competitors for its goods in the US market. External Affairs Minister Jaishankar said a few days back that the trade talks between the two sides are nearing a "landing point". The India-US relations witnessed a major downturn after Washington imposed punitive tariffs on India last year and President Trump made assertions regarding his role in de-escalating the India-Pakistan military clashes of May 2025 that drew sharp reaction from Indian officials. Washington's new immigration policy and its decision to increase H1B visa fees also contributed to the slide in India-US ties. The ties came under fresh strain after the US decided to restrict a key green-card processing programme for major global and Indian IT firms, including Tata Consultancy Services and Wipro.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Quietly Rewrote Law On Alibi
stories.title: Supreme Court Quietly Rewrote Law On Alibi
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: A quiet but consequential shift just occurred in Indian criminal procedure, and it happened in a case that, on its surface, looks like a routine mercy for a soldier.
In Rahul.

State of Uttar Pradesh (Criminal Appeal arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 2939 of 2026, decided on 11 August 2026), Rahul, a Border Security Force jawan, was posted on the Indo-Bangladesh border when his wife died at her matrimonial home in Meerut.
He, his parents, and other relatives were booked for dowry death.
His parents went to trial and, after years of proceedings, were acquitted, the prosecution couldn't prove its case.
The Allahabad High Court held that an alibi is a matter for trial, not something a court can weigh on paper, before evidence is tested, before witnesses are cross-examined.

The Supreme Court disagreed, reviving a line with far-reaching implications: that where a defence document is of "sterling and unimpeachable quality" and it "completely demolishes the prosecution case," the High Courts can quash such proceedings before trial even begins.
This instance unsettles a rule that has protected criminal trials for decades, and every criminal lawyer now has reason to pay attention.

An alibi doesn't just deny guilt; it claims physical impossibility, "I could not have done this, because I was elsewhere." Because that claim can be faked as easily as it can be true, the law has always required it to be proved "with absolute certainty," at trial, where the document can be tested, and the other side gets a real chance to challenge it.
A court asked to quash a case beforehand has traditionally been told not to play judge on a paper nobody has had the chance to contest.
This idea that some documents are too solid to argue about did not begin with this particular case.
It traces back to 1992, when the Supreme Court in State of Haryana.

stories.headline: IMD update: Isolated very heavy rain for TN, Puducherry for two more days
stories.title: IMD update: Isolated very heavy rain for TN, Puducherry for two more days
stories.summary: India Meteorological Department’s numerical projections indicate possibility of rapid intensification of the Bay system into a tropical cyclone, although it has yet to take an official call on this
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Isolated very heavy rainfall is forecast over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on Wednesday and Thursday, as the India Meteorological Department (IMD) watches the possible formation of two low-pressure areas at opposite ends of the Bay of Bengal, one of which could likely intensify into a tropical cyclone.
The first low is expected to form over the south-west Bay and adjoining Tamil Nadu coast on Wednesday, as a cyclonic circulation descends to lower atmospheric levels.
The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) had earlier suggested the system could instead form over the south-east Arabian Sea.
The second system is expected to emerge from an incoming circulation over the Gulf of Thailand and adjoining parts of Thailand and Myanmar.
Moving into the north Andaman Sea by Wednesday, it is forecast to travel west-north-west and form a low over the south-east and adjoining east-central Bay by Friday.
It could then turn north-westwards towards the Andhra Pradesh coast and intensify further.
IMD’s numerical projections indicate possibility of its rapid intensification over the warm waters into a tropical cyclone, although it has yet to take an official call.

Global model forecasts, including those of the ECMWF, broadly support this scenario, against the backdrop of an active north-east monsoon, a passing helpful Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) wave over Indian Ocean and a developing positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) phase.
The evolving systems are already influencing regional weather.
On Tuesday evening, an elongated trough of low pressure extended from the circulation over south-west Bay and adjoining Tamil Nadu coast towards north coastal Andhra Pradesh.
Its southern flanks overlapped the leading edge of an easterly wave advancing from the Andaman Sea, within which the incoming disturbance from the Gulf of Thailand is expected to be embedded.
The IMD has issued a fishermen’s warning for the Andaman Sea for three days from Friday, coinciding with the anticipated intensification phase of the system embedded in the easterly wave.
